guidelineVersions: EHS emergency ventral and incisional hernia guidelines (JAWS, 2026)
EHS classification of abdominal wall hernias (Hernia, 2009)

related.why: Parastomal hernia and old stoma sites

brief.scenario: Mrs Janice Holbrook, 64, had an emergency laparotomy for perforated diverticulitis three years ago; her wound became infected. For a year she has had a swelling at her scar that aches by the evening and is bigger when she stands. A chaperone is available.
brief.task: Examine her abdominal wall. You will be stopped at 6 minutes to present your findings and answer questions.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Standing then lying; the whole scar; cough impulse, reducibility, tenderness; head lift to find the defect edges; the rest of the abdominal wall.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Examining only the obvious bulge and missing a second defect or an old stoma-site hernia.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "Could you stand for me first? I'll look at the whole of your tummy."

grid.label: Consent and exposure
grid.fail: Examines through clothing, or exposes her without explanation or chaperone offer.
grid.pass: Explains, gains consent, offers a chaperone, and exposes from the lower chest to the groins.
grid.high: Asks whether the lump is painful now before touching it, and keeps her covered where possible.

grid.label: Inspection standing and lying
grid.pass: Inspects standing, then lying: scars, the swelling, skin changes (thinning, redness, ulceration), and a cough impulse.
grid.high: Asks her to lift her head off the pillow to tense the recti, showing the defect and separating it from divarication.

grid.label: Palpation
grid.fail: Pushes hard to reduce a tender lump.
grid.pass: Checks tenderness, temperature and cough impulse; asks her to reduce it; feels the edges of the fascial defect.
grid.high: Estimates defect width and uses the EHS width classes: W1 under 4 cm, W2 4–10 cm, W3 10 cm or more.

grid.label: The rest of the abdominal wall
grid.pass: Examines the full scar length, old drain and stoma sites, the umbilicus and both groins; listens over the swelling.
grid.high: Notes skin quality and whether the contents seem to live outside the abdomen, which affect repair planning.

grid.label: Presentation at the signal
grid.pass: Presents a reducible, non-tender midline incisional hernia, with site, size and estimated defect width.
grid.high: Links her risk factors: previous wound infection, obesity and smoking; mentions divarication as a differential.

grid.label: Imaging
grid.pass: CT (or MRI) to plan surgery; imaging to confirm the diagnosis if examination is uncertain.
grid.high: States CT is the most sensitive test; ultrasound or MRI with Valsalva if radiation or cost is a concern.

grid.label: Elective management
grid.fail: Says every incisional hernia needs urgent repair, or ignores optimisation.
grid.pass: Discusses watchful waiting versus repair based on quality of life; optimises weight, diabetes and smoking; mesh repair if operating.
grid.high: Quotes acute complication risk about 1% at 1 year and 2.5% at 5 years; retromuscular mesh with defect closure.

grid.label: Emergency presentation (safety-critical)
grid.fail: Books a clinic for a tender, irreducible hernia with vomiting.
grid.pass: Tender, irreducible hernia with obstruction: resuscitate, nil by mouth, bloods, CT, senior review, emergency surgery.
grid.high: EHS emergency guidance: damage control if unstable; mesh-based repair where the defect can be closed, whatever the contamination grade; staged if not.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Lie down and lift your top, please. [No explanation or chaperone offer.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Presses firmly on the lump.] Let me push it back. [She winces.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: A lump on her tummy near the scar.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: List her for urgent repair; she doesn't need a scan.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: If it became tender and irreducible and she was vomiting?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'd see her in clinic next week.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Hello, I'm Dr Patel, one of the surgical trainees. Can I check your name and date of birth? I'd like to examine your tummy and scar, from your lower chest to your groins. Would you like a chaperone? [Consent; cleans hands.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Could you stand? [Inspects: scars, swelling, skin.] Cough, please. [Impulse.] Now lie down. [Inspects again.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Is it sore? Could you push it back? [Reduces.] [Feels defect edges.] About 6 cm across.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Full scar length, old stoma site, umbilicus, both groins; listens over the swelling.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Mrs Holbrook has a reducible, non-tender midline incisional hernia in the upper part of her laparotomy scar, with an estimated 6 cm defect.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: A CT to plan surgery. It aches daily, so I'd discuss repair against watchful waiting, help her lose weight and stop smoking first, and use a mesh repair if we operate.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: If it became tender and irreducible and she was vomiting?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Obstruction or strangulation: resuscitate, nil by mouth, bloods, CT, senior review and emergency surgery.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Hello, I'm Dr Patel. Can I check your name and date of birth? Is the lump sore right now? [No.] I'll keep you covered where I can.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Standing and lying.] Could you lift your head off the pillow? [Defect edges show; the recti are otherwise together.] That's a hernia, not a divarication.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Reduces; defect edges.] About 6 cm wide, so W2 in the EHS classification.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Whole wall.] The skin is healthy, and the contents stay reducible, so it isn't losing domain.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: A reducible midline incisional hernia, W2. Her risk factors are the wound infection, her weight and smoking.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: CT is the most sensitive and helps plan repair; ultrasound or MRI with Valsalva if radiation is a concern.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Not necessarily. The risk of an acute complication is about 1% at 1 year and 2.5% at 5 years, so it depends on her quality of life. If we repair it: optimise first, close the defect and place a retromuscular mesh.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Resuscitate, CT and emergency surgery. EHS emergency guidance favours damage control if she's unstable, and mesh-based repair where the defect can be closed, whatever the contamination grade, after source control if contaminated. If it can't be closed, a staged repair.

failures.consequence: The hernia reduces and is under-called.
Misses a second defect along the scar or at an old stoma site.

failures.move: Listing every incisional hernia for surgery without optimisation.
failures.consequence: Higher wound complication and recurrence risk in smokers and obese patients.

failures.move: Treating a tender, irreducible hernia with vomiting as routine.

recovery.line: Could you stand up for me? The swelling may disappear when you lie down.

recovery.when: Unsure if it's a hernia or divarication
recovery.line: I'd ask her to lift her head: a divarication bulges along the midline without a discrete defect edge.

knowledge.fact: Risk factors: high BMI, smoking, diabetes, immunosuppression, midline incision; surgical site infection has the largest impact.
Reducible incisional hernia: acute complication about 1% at 1 year, 2.5% at 5 years; repair if symptoms affect quality of life.
Pre-optimise: weight, HbA1c, smoking cessation (over 4 weeks), fitness. Midline repair: close the defect, retromuscular mesh.
EHS width: W1 under 4 cm, W2 4–10 cm, W3 10 cm or more.

recall.think: Is it tender and irreducible? Is there more than one defect?
recall.say: "Reducible midline incisional hernia, defect about 6 cm."
do: Reduce; feel defect edges; head lift

numbers.meaning: acute complication risk at 1 and 5 years

recall.trap: Not every incisional hernia needs surgery; optimise first.
recall.finish: Optimise, CT planning, mesh repair if symptomatic; emergency surgery if strangulated.

sources.name: Sanders DL, Pawlak MM, et al. Midline incisional hernia guidelines: the European Hernia Society. Br J Surg 2023;110(12):1732–68
sources.supports: Risk factors (high BMI, smoking, diabetes, immunosuppression, midline incision; SSI largest impact); imaging if examination is not definitive, CT most sensitive, ultrasound or MRI with Valsalva if cost or radiation a concern; CT or MRI for preoperative planning; reducible hernia: acute hernia accident about 1% in the first year and 2.5% by 5 years; repair when symptoms adversely affect quality of life after discussing watchful waiting; pre-optimisation (weight, HbA1c, smoking cessation, pulmonary fitness), smoking cessation over 4 weeks; mesh-based repair recommended; retromuscular mesh; close the fascial defect, avoid bridging

sources.name: Muysoms FE, et al. Classification of primary and incisional abdominal wall hernias. Hernia 2009;13(4):407–14
sources.supports: Incisional hernia width classes: W1 under 4 cm, W2 4 to 10 cm, W3 10 cm or more

sources.name: Stabilini C, Theodorou A, Pawlak M, et al. EHS guidelines on the management of primary ventral and incisional hernias under emergency conditions. J Abdom Wall Surg 2026;5:16228 (PMID 41938186)
sources.supports: Damage-control approach prioritising physiological stability; mesh-based repair suggested over primary fascial closure where the defect can be closed, whatever the contamination grade (CDC I, and CDC II or above once source control is achieved); staged repair, deferring definitive reconstruction, for large defects not amenable to closure

partner.opening: Please examine this lady's abdominal wall. A chaperone is available. I'll stop you at 6 minutes.
partner.actorBrief: You are Mrs Janice Holbrook, 64. Emergency bowel operation three years ago for a burst diverticulum; the wound got infected and took weeks to heal. You had a stoma that was later reversed. For a year a lump at the top of your scar aches by the evening and gets bigger when you stand. You smoke 15 a day and have been told you are overweight. No vomiting; bowels normal. Push the lump back yourself when asked.

reveals.trigger: Inspects standing and asks her to cough
reveals.finding: Long midline laparotomy scar and a healed left iliac fossa stoma scar. 8 cm swelling in the upper part of the midline scar, bigger on standing, with a visible cough impulse. Skin healthy.

reveals.trigger: Palpates and asks her to reduce it
reveals.finding: Non-tender, not warm. Reduces fully lying. Fascial defect edges palpable, about 6 cm across.
Defect edges become clearer; no separation of the recti elsewhere.

reveals.trigger: Examines the rest of the wall
reveals.finding: No hernia at the old stoma site, umbilicus or groins. Bowel sounds normal over the swelling.
Say: "Please stop there and present your findings."

push.question: How do you tell an incisional hernia from divarication?
push.expect: Head lift: divarication bulges along the midline without a discrete defect edge.

push.question: Would you image her?
push.expect: CT to plan surgery; CT most sensitive if the diagnosis is uncertain.

push.question: Should she have an operation?
push.expect: Depends on quality of life; optimise weight and smoking first; mesh repair.

curveballs.prompt: The swelling is tender and irreducible, and she has vomited three times.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Obstructed or strangulated: resuscitate, nil by mouth, bloods, CT, senior review, emergency surgery.

curveballs.prompt: She says it hardly bothers her.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Watchful waiting is reasonable: low acute risk; advise her to return with pain, irreducibility or vomiting.

curveballs.prompt: She has been told she needs to lose weight first but hasn't managed to.
curveballs.safeAnswer: If a dedicated programme fails, the risks of delay may outweigh further waiting: discuss repair.

curveballs.prompt: She asks why she got it.
curveballs.safeAnswer: The wound infection is the biggest factor; smoking and weight also contribute.
